title: The Natural Minor Scale
description: Play A natural minor, the white-key minor scale, and the minor chords that grow out of it.

steps.title: Same keys, different home
steps.description: The natural minor scale has a darker, more serious sound than major. Its pattern is whole, half, whole, whole, half, whole, whole (W-H-W-W-H-W-W). Start that pattern on A and you get A, B, C, D, E, F, G: the same white keys as C major. Only the home note has changed.

steps.title: Find A
steps.description: Press A4 to get your bearings. A is the white key between the second and third black keys in a group of three.
steps.hint: From middle C, count up the white keys: C, D, E, F, G, A.

steps.title: Now the scale
steps.description: Play up from A: A, B, C, D, E, F, G. All white keys, but listen to how different it feels when A is home.
steps.hint: Any octave works. Start on A and walk up the white keys to G.

steps.title: A minor chord
steps.description: Play A, C and E together. This is the home chord of A minor.
steps.hint: Thumb on A, middle finger on C, pinky on E.

steps.title: D minor chord
steps.description: Play D, F and A. In A minor, this is chord iv. The numeral is lowercase because the chord is minor.
steps.hint: D, F, A. Skip one white key between each.

steps.title: E minor chord
steps.description: Play E, G and B. This is chord v in A minor. Afterwards, try A minor, D minor, E minor, A minor in a row and hear how they hang together.
steps.hint: E, G, B. Same skip-a-key shape.

steps.title: Whole and half steps
steps.description: Which step pattern gives you a natural minor scale?
